The provided text explores the tension between societal expectations and personal desires in *Pride and Prejudice*, highlighting how different reader backgrounds shape their interpretation of the narrative. Feminist readers are likely to view Elizabeth Bennet as an emblem of female agency, prioritizing individual autonomy and resistance to patriarchal constraints. In contrast, traditionalist readers may place greater emphasis on the structural importance of social standing and family reputation, viewing these elements as essential components of social stability and moral order. This divergence illustrates how a single literary work can resonate differently depending on the ideological lens through which it is read.

Regarding the priority question: The primary use of a bed is for sleeping.
